reasoning:
I'm weighing whether to merge the three per-color fields into one goal-ordered list, since green_cube_pos went unread here but would matter if the goal named green. The necessity condition still holds since an ordered list counts as one field, one fact, so this refactor seems like a reasonable way to trim memory to what's truly needed.

Now I'm drafting the exact edits: updating the subgoal instruction that records each cube's position to instead record goal_cube_positions as the ordered [y, x] list per the goal's naming order, and revising the retrieval instruction so the target position is looked up from that list by index rather than from the separate color fields.

policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_from: The target is the cube named in the goal at position picks_done+1 in the goal's order (first named cube when picks_done is 0, second named cube when picks_done is 1). policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_to: The target position is the entry of goal_cube_positions at index picks_done (first entry when picks_done is 0, second entry when picks_done is 1). Point at the center of the container nearest to that recorded position

policy_prompt_for_memory.description: Ordered list of the [y, x] positions of the cubes the goal instruction names, in the goal's order. If this step shows loose cubes and no containers anywhere (the scene before the button is pressed), read the goal, take each cube it names in order, and write that cube's [y, x] as shown; skip cubes the goal does not name. Otherwise copy the carried-in list unchanged; never overwrite an entry from a cube briefly exposed under a lifted container. e.g. [[78, 157], [106, 105]] when the goal names blue then red.

annotator_prompt.description: Ordered list of the [y, x] positions of the cubes named in the goal instruction, in the order the goal names them, as those cubes were seen at step #1 (t=0) while loose and before any container has come down. One entry per cube the goal names (one entry for a one-container goal, two for a two-container goal); cubes the goal does not name are not recorded. Written at step #1 and held unchanged for the rest of the episode, even after a cube is hidden by a container or briefly re-exposed when a container is lifted. e.g. [[78, 157], [106, 105]] for a goal that names the blue cube then the red cube.
